reuse.why: The tree already exports getScheduledAmount (missing/number/range dispatch, used by the desktop client); the change introduces a parallel getExpectedAmount with the same dispatch instead of extending it, reusing only getApproxNumberThreshold.

duplication.why: getExpectedAmount re-implements getScheduledAmount's null/number/range dispatch, and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions keeps its own null/number ternary around the new helper.

placement.why: The amount rule lives in shared/schedules.ts and server sites import it, which matches the tree's layering; the API field is added in the scheduleModel mapper.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule and API field, though several updated comments are left stating the superseded 'furthest from zero' rule.

maintainability.why: Two exported definitions of the expected amount now disagree on approximate amounts (client callers of getScheduledAmount never see the tolerance), so the next rule change has to find both, plus a redundant dispatch at the preview site and stale comments.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts: new getExpectedAmount sits beside the existing getScheduledAmount instead of extending it; computeSchedulePreviewTransactions bypasses getExpectedAmount's own null/number handling

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts getExpectedAmount: getScheduledAmount's missing/number/range dispatch renamed and reshaped (inverse dropped, op added) rather than merged

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedAmount gains the op parameter and an isapprox branch; computeSchedulePreviewTransactions keeps its own null/number dispatch, and getScheduledAmount (desktop client callers) remains a second path that applies only the range rule
